newsitem.title: USA: U.S.-French air alliances hinge on open skies-DOT.
newsitem.headline: U.S.-French air alliances hinge on open skies-DOT.

text.p: Alliances between U.S. and French airlines cannot develop until a firm bilateral aviation agreement exists between the two countries, a U.S. Department of Transportation official told a House committee Thursday.

"Until an acceptable level of agreement is in place, we are not prepared to approve codesharing relationships or strategic alliances for French carriers, or allow them to have significant capacity increases," said Charles Hunnicutt, the department's assistant secretary for aviation and international affairs.
Codesharing allows carriers to easily market tickets on each other's flights.

Hunnicutt said alliances between airlines in the United States and European countries other than France had demonstrated the potential benefits of such relationships for the airlines and nations involved.
The United States has pushed for a three-year transition period leading to "open skies" in France, while the French would prefer a nine-year delay, Hunnicutt told a House Transportation subcommittee.
"We have made little progress with France in negotiating a new open aviation agreement which I believe Air France must have if it is to continue as a major player on the world stage," he said.
